scope: Read-only source analysis; no service/model imports, live requests, new log polling, tests, process changes, or frozen-helper edits.
cause: worker_once sets the future result and writes completed before acquiring the condition lock in finally to clear _active/_inflight. submit and release_waiter hold that condition lock while writing their own receipt. ReceiptWriter has a separate lock and fsync may release the GIL. Therefore the gateway can observe the old active/inflight job while completed is being written and append its waiter record immediately afterward.
record_note: These are schematic lifecycle fields, not fabricated runtime receipts. Actual records must retain all current metadata and pass receipt_id canonical hash validation.
thread_schedule: Model worker has finished generation/check-in, sets future result, begins writing completed under the receipt-writer lock.
Gateway admits same-key same-fingerprint retry, acquires condition lock, sees the existing _inflight job, increments waiter_count, then waits for the receipt-writer lock.
Model worker finishes completed/fsync and releases writer lock; it cannot clear _active/_inflight because gateway still owns condition lock.
Gateway writes coalesced, returns the already-completed shared future, releases condition lock; worker then clears the old active/inflight entry.
disconnect_variant: Replace retry with cancellation of the sole remaining HTTP waiter: release_waiter finds _active, reduces waiter_count to zero, future.cancel() returns false because the future already completed, but the implementation still appends disconnected_active. Thus queued, selected, completed(delivered), disconnected_active is also possible.
current_parser_result: _qos_selected sets active=None at completed and then rejects either late waiter event as waiter event without active/pending work. This is a false rejection of successful drain evidence, not false acceptance or a lost check-in.
narrow_proposal: Keep current pending/active/selected/completed accounting and all success/error/hash requirements.

Track only the most recent successfully completed sequence as eligible for late waiter bookkeeping until the next selected event or another worker-only post-cleanup event (queue_timeout or stopped_pending). Queued requests for other sequences need not close the window.

Permit coalesced/disconnected_active for that one sequence without changing active state, generation counts, matched check-in pairs, or recorded completion outcome. Preserve these records separately as late waiter bookkeeping.
Never permit an unknown sequence, failed generation, second completion, or an older completed sequence after a newer selection.
proposed_tests: Model-free coordinator concurrency characterization using explicit thread barriers around completion receipt writing reproduces the realistic interleaving without inference/model work.
Parser accepts successful completion followed by same-sequence coalesced or disconnected_active, including an unrelated queued event between them.
Parser rejects unknown late sequence, old sequence after a subsequent selection, missing selected/queued, duplicate completion, failed completion, and unresolved pending/active work.
